Source and correction of segregation drift¶

Where the drift came from¶

There were three discretisation errors, rather than accumulated floating-point roundoff. Particle-to-grid deposition already conserved species mass.

The wrong global quantity was conserved. The previous KT update telescoped sum_i delta_phi[i,k] to zero. The total particle inventory is instead Q[k] = sum_p m[p]*phi[p,k]. The former incremental gather obeys

delta_Q[k] = sum_i M[i]*delta_phi[i,k]

because M[i] = sum_p m[p]*N[p,i]. Therefore an unweighted concentration sum is insufficient when nodal masses differ. In the slope fixture, boundary nodes carry 13.5 kg and interior nodes 27 kg. On the very first bidisperse timestep, particle-to-grid mass error is zero, but the old update changes the two species by approximately +6.78e-7 kg and -6.78e-7 kg. The error accumulates after that. Periodic duplicate endpoints must also count only once in this identity.

Diffusion was multiplied by concentration twice. KT2_flux returned v[k] - D*grad(phi[k]) and the KT routine treated that entire quantity as a velocity, multiplying it by the reconstructed phi[k]. The resulting diffusion flux was -D*phi[k]*grad(phi[k]), rather than -D*grad(phi[k]). Summing the former over species is generally nonzero even when the fractions sum to one.

The mixture was discretised as independent scalar equations. Each class got a different numerical diffusion speed and an independently limited slope. Those operations do not preserve sum_k delta_phi[i,k] = 0. Physical segregation velocities do sum to zero when weighted by composition; that identity must also hold for the numerical face flux, including its stabilisation terms.

The old conservation test used uniform M[i] = 1 and checked only global sums. It could not detect the first error and did not check local mixture closure.

Corrected grid update¶

The relative concentration flux retains the intended segregation and diffusion coefficients:

F[k] = c*phi[k]*(1/(s[k]*sum_j(phi[j]/s[j])) - 1)*grad(pk)
       - D*grad(phi[k])

A scalar limiter is shared across the whole reconstructed mixture. Both sides of a face use one common numerical speed, bounded by the advective Jacobian row norm. Physical diffusion uses the cell-centre concentration difference separately from advection and numerical stabilisation. These choices preserve zero total relative mixture flux without selecting a special dependent grain class.

Each face exchanges a species-mass vector T[k], rather than evolving an unweighted concentration. Flux density uses the harmonic mean of adjacent mobile mass densities, M[i]/V[i], and the face’s actual area. Boundary control volumes have half widths. Closed boundaries block exterior faces; empty nodes and internal walls block transport through their normal faces. Periodic faces are evaluated once, then copied to the display endpoint.

The same T[k] is removed from one node and added to its neighbour. Thus each species is globally conservative. Concentration increments are obtained by dividing the resulting nodal mass increments by the participating nodal mass. Rigid particles are excluded from both the transport inventory and the return transfer.

Bounded return to particles¶

The original FLIP-style concentration increment can make a particle’s depleted grain class negative, even if the nodal mixture remains positive. A limiter based only on that gather was too restrictive: it could freeze diffusion across pure layers. The corrected return transfer uses the actual species inventories.

For a face carrying class k from node i, its donor weights are

donor[p,i,k] = m[p]*N[p,i]*phi[p,k] / Q[i,k]

where Q[i,k] is the deposited mobile species mass. A donor particle loses only grains it owns and receives equal mass from the counter-flowing classes on that face. Each particle’s total mass stays fixed, and the opposite side receives the same species masses. For uniform composition this reduces to the original incremental gather. When physical and numerical fluxes are zero, particle composition is unchanged: there is no unconditional PIC smoothing.

Outgoing demand is budgeted over all faces in both directions before updating. One factor per face limits every class together, so limiting preserves both species conservation and zero mixture flux. A small floating-point balance of oppositely signed face totals precedes the return transfer. Fractions are never clipped or renormalised by this algorithm.

The grid API is now G.calculate_phi_increment(P, L) for the coupled update. It stages both G.dphi and inventory-aware particle increments. The main timestep and benchmark driver pass L. Calling it without L, or calling increment_grainsize(P, G), returns the standalone grid update; its caller is responsible for its explicit timestep stability.

Verification¶

Checks include nonuniform nodal/particle masses, local fraction sums, coupled species inventories, rigid particles, free surfaces, closed and periodic faces, class-order permutation, both spatial directions, pure-layer mixing, and transport steps far beyond the unbounded explicit update. A node-aligned sinusoidal mixture reproduces the discrete heat-equation step for constant diffusivity. The slope examples also run for 1,000 steps with normalisation off.

Raw measurements are in benchmarks/segregation_drift_before.json and benchmarks/segregation_drift.json. Regenerate the corrected report with python -m benchmarks.segregation_drift. The small performance snapshot is separate from the historical conversion benchmarks.

These checks establish conservation, bounds, and specific diffusion behaviour; they do not validate the segregation constitutive law against experiments. The existing diffusion coefficient’s zero-inertial-number convention remains unchanged. Limiting can reduce transport when particle inventories cannot supply a proposed exchange, so quantitative predictions still require mesh/timestep convergence checks.

The central-upwind framework and its reconstruction/flux distinction are described by Kurganov and Lin (2007). The defects and corrections above were established directly from this code and the independent conservation/physics checks, rather than attributed to the paper.
